research_mode: official HSE and GOV.UK primary guidance only; gas, asbestos, smoke/carbon-monoxide alarm and residential fire-safety regulatory and methodology gates; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Gas-safety landlord definition
verified_claims: For domestic gas duties, HSE describes a landlord as someone renting property under a lease shorter than seven years or under a licence.
limitations: Other legislation may use a different landlord definition, and legal status cannot be inferred from parcel ownership alone.

sources.name: Gas-safety accommodation coverage
verified_claims: Landlord gas-safety duties cover a broad range of rented accommodation, including local-authority, housing-association, private, hostel, bed-sit, hotel and holiday accommodation.
limitations: The listed examples do not prove that a specific tenancy falls within scope.

sources.name: Landlord tenant gas-safety duty
verified_claims: Landlords are responsible for tenant safety under the Gas Safety (Installation and Use) Regulations 1998 for gas appliances, fittings and flues they provide.
limitations: A general statutory duty is not evidence of compliance or non-compliance at a named property.

sources.name: Communal gas appliance scope
verified_claims: Gas appliances, fittings and flues in communal areas that tenants may use are included in landlord duties.
limitations: Communal-area coverage does not identify which installations exist in a specific building.

sources.name: Letting-agent gas duty transfer
verified_claims: Where a contract gives an agent responsibility, the same relevant gas-safety duties apply to that agent.
limitations: Contractual allocation must be established from the actual agreement and cannot be assumed.

sources.name: Gas Safe maintenance requirement
verified_claims: Maintenance and repair of landlord-provided gas pipework, appliances and flues must be arranged through a Gas Safe registered engineer.
limitations: The requirement does not prove that a named engineer or installation is registered or compliant.

sources.name: Annual landlord gas-safety check
verified_claims: Landlords must arrange a gas-safety check every 12 months by a Gas Safe registered engineer.
limitations: An annual interval does not establish the date or result of a specific property's latest check.

sources.name: Early gas-check timing flexibility
verified_claims: The 2018 amendment allows an annual gas-safety check in the two months before its due date while retaining the existing expiry date.
limitations: The flexibility does not extend the maximum statutory cycle beyond the permitted schedule.

sources.name: Gas-safety record retention
verified_claims: Landlords must keep gas-safety check records for two years.
limitations: A retention duty does not prove that records exist or are complete for a named tenancy.

sources.name: Existing-tenant gas record delivery
verified_claims: A copy of the gas-safety record must be issued to each existing tenant within 28 days of the check.
limitations: The deadline cannot be evaluated without the actual check and delivery dates.

sources.name: New-tenant gas record delivery
verified_claims: New tenants must receive a copy of the gas-safety record before moving in.
limitations: The duty does not establish whether a particular tenant received the document.

sources.name: Tenant-owned gas appliance boundary
verified_claims: For a tenant-owned gas appliance not supplied by the landlord, the landlord retains duties for associated installation pipework but not the appliance itself.
limitations: Ownership and installation boundaries require property-specific evidence.

sources.name: Communal-building gas evidence chain
verified_claims: A landlord within a larger building should ensure communal gas appliances, flues and pipework are maintained and checked by the building owner and that evidence is available.
limitations: The guidance does not prove that building-owner evidence has been obtained for a specific block.

sources.name: Long-lease gas-duty boundary
verified_claims: HSE states that where a lease is longer than seven years and for life, the landlord is not responsible for gas-safety checks and maintenance under this duty.
limitations: Lease duration and legal form must be confirmed from the actual lease.

sources.name: Gas amendment safety-standard preservation
verified_claims: HSE states that the 2018 timing changes do not relax regulatory requirements or reduce safety standards.
limitations: The statement is about the amendment and does not certify any individual installation.
